visible_support.text: Retain the previously supplied give-to-drink pattern: sęle mē wæter drincan. Sęle is the singular command give, mē the recipient, wæter the thing given; the plain infinitive, without tō, expresses what the recipient is to do. The whole construction remains supplied.
Cook supplies ācenned, born (past participle), with plain e. Use with the taught passive auxiliary; this exact hint does not establish a complete ācennan system.

Flēoð is third plural present indicative of flēon, flee; it is not the verb fly. Ðǣr, there; næddran, snakes/adders, nominative plural of weak feminine næddre; onwęg, away. Both d letters in næddran belong to the printed text.

Read the whole opening as “then, after a long time, it happened that ...”. Æfter governs the dative; langum fæce means a long interval. The opening ðæt belongs to this supplied time-introduction frame.

The ðæt clause gives his purpose. Wolde with the infinitives scēawian and gesēon is read here “that he might watch and see” or “in order to watch and see”; do not make private desire the only force. Hwæt ūs gelumpe is a dependent question, what might happen to us. Gelumpe is third singular preterite subjunctive, and ūs is dative.

Gebed is prayer, accusative singular; gefylde is the already taught finished/accomplished. Samod ætgædere means together/at once. Paired ge ... ge coordinates both ... and; the first ge introduces the sea-calming and the second the storm-stilling.

Gesyndge is the exact syncopated source form beside taught gesyndige, favorable, nominative plural. Smyltestan is the weak masculine accusative superlative calmest/very calm. Ðurh governs ðone ... sǣ; ūs is the accusative people brought. Æt lande means to/at land in this exact arrival expression. Gebrōhton is the prefixed third plural preterite brought.

The temporal clause has the two completed actions: we came up onto land and carried our ship up from the waves. Lande is the locally supplied dative of land; ȳðum is dative plural waves after fram. Ābǣron is first plural preterite of prefixed carry. Ūre scip is the accusative object, not a new subject.

Sōna, immediately; ęft, again; hwearf, returned. Se-ðe is the exact relative complex referring to masculine storm. For ūrum intingan, for our sake; intingan is dative singular. Medmicel fæc is accusative duration, a short interval. Gestilde is intransitive ceased/became still in this relative clause; the earlier transitive sense alone is insufficient. English had ceased may clarify the sequence.

Fierst is masculine nominative singular, interval/period; medmicla is its weak adjective, short. Ðǣre stilnesse, of the calm, is genitive singular. In the relative clause, ðǣr means there and becōm means occurred/came about in this context.
